extracted.intended_audience: small businesses and Principal Investigators preparing SBIR/STTR Phase I proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing the commercialization portion of a Phase I SBIR/STTR proposal, summarizing what major federal agencies expect (DoD, DOE, HHS, NSF, NASA) and procedural requirements for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common evaluation criteria: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three criteria commonly considered important in evaluating all SBIR/STTR proposals: Innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tutorial previously introduced Innovation as a core evaluation dimension; check the current solicitation/FOA for agency-specific emphasis and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common evaluation criteria: Capabilities of the team
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three criteria commonly considered important in evaluating all SBIR/STTR proposals: Capabilities of the team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate team qualifications and capacity to carry out the proposed work; consult the FOA for any component-specific expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common evaluation criteria: Commercialization
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three criteria commonly considered important in evaluating all SBIR/STTR proposals: Commercialization (as defined in the SBIR and STTR Policy Directives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercialization is defined in the SBIR/STTR Policy Directives. Although brief, the definition encompasses many aspects; consult the directives and the specific FOA for agency expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD: Commercialization Strategy (approx. 1 page)
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD requests a section called Commercialization Strategy, approximately 1 page in length in the Technical Proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance to proposers: "Describe…. your company's strategy for commercializing this technology in DoD, other Federal Agencies, and/or private sector markets. Provide specific information on the market need the technology will address and the size of the market. Also include a schedule showing the quantitative commercialization results from this SBIR project that your company expects to achieve." Note that each DoD component may have additional guidance; review both the DoD Instructions (Preface) and component-specific documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE: Two-page Commercialization Plan; mandatory upload
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE requests a two page Commercialization Plan uploaded through Grants.gov in the Other- Phase I Commercialization Plan section of the Funding Opportunity Announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOE has increased emphasis on commercialization for Phase I/II. Warning from DOE: "If the Commercialization Plan is not included at the time of application submission, your application will be administratively declined without review." DOE also provides an example Phase I Commercialization Plan on its website — use it as a template for responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS: Significance section must address marketability; separate plan for Fast Track
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS emphasizes commercialization in Phase II; for Phase I, Fast Track applicants submitting combined Phase I/II must include a separate commercialization plan. All Phase I applicants must address commercialization potential within the Research Plan's Significance section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the Research Plan under Significance, applicants are asked to: "Explain the importance of the problem or critical barrier to progress in the field that the proposed project addresses" and "to explain the project's potential to lead to a marketable product, process, or service." For Fast Track/Phase II, include the separate HHS commercialization plan as specified in HHS guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF: Commercial Opportunity discussion (2–4 pages recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF asks applicants to discuss the Commercial Opportunity in the Project Description and recommends spending two to four pages on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF recommends addressing items such as: "Is there a broader societal need you are trying to address with this commercial opportunity? Please describe." "Describe the market and addressable market for the innovation. Discuss the business economics and market drivers in the target industry." "How has the market opportunity been validated?" "Describe your customers and your basic business model." Use these prompts to structure market, customer, validation, and business-model content in the Project Description.

rubrics_metrics.name: NASA: Potential Post Application / initial commercialization strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA requires a Potential Post Application section as part of the Technical Proposal that addresses potential applications and initial commercialization strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASA guidance: "The Phase I proposal shall (1) forecast the potential and targeted application(s) of the proposed innovation and associated products and services relative to NASA needs (infusion into NASA mission needs and projects), other Government agencies and commercial markets, (2) identify potential customers, and (3) provide an initial commercialization strategy that addresses key technical, market and business factors for the successful development, demonstration and utilization of the innovation and associated products and services." Note: NASA uses the term "infusion" to mean adoption of technology within NASA. Also: "Commercialization encompasses the transition of technology into products and services for NASA mission programs, other Government agencies, and non-Government markets."

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural/format requirement: check solicitation for placement and attachment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercialization requirements vary by agency and solicitation: sometimes the commercialization content is part of the Technical Proposal; other times it is a separate attachment uploaded in a specified FOA section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before drafting, review the solicitation/FOA to determine whether commercialization content should be embedded in the Research/Project Description or uploaded as a separate Commercialization Plan attachment, and to confirm page limits, upload locations, and any mandatory language or formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult agency-specific examples and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use agency-provided examples and component guidance to prepare responsive commercialization materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tutorial highlights that DOE provides an example Phase I Commercialization Plan and that DoD components may provide additional component-specific guidance. Always consult the current FOA and agency resources to align content, length, and required elements.
